title.zh: 卷二十一 列傳第二 文惠太子
title.raw: 卷二十一 列傳第二 文惠太子 Volume 21 Biographies 2: Crown Prince Wenhui

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷二十一‧列傳第二

translations.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 21 — Biographies 2
translations.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 21 — Biographies 2

sentences.zh: 文惠太子

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhui

sentences.zh: 文惠太子長懋字雲喬，世祖長子也。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui Zhangmao, courtesy name Yunqiao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhui, Xiao Zhangmao, courtesy name Yunqiao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 世祖年未弱冠而生太子，爲太祖所愛。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had not yet come of age when the crown prince was born, and the Grand Ancestor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was not yet twenty when Xiao Zhangmao was born, and Xiao Daocheng, the Grand Ancestor, doted on him.

sentences.zh: 姿容豐潤，小字白澤。

translations.literal: His bearing was full and fair; his childhood name was Baize.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome and well favored; in childhood he was called Baize.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽末，隨世祖在郢。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuánhuī era of Song, he followed Emperor Wu at Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuánhuī era of Song he was with Emperor Wu at Ying.

sentences.zh: 世祖還鎮盆城拒沈攸之，使太子勞接將帥，親侍軍旅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu returned to garrison at Pencheng to resist Shen Youzhi, he had the crown prince greet the generals and take part in the army in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu went back to hold Pencheng against Shen Youzhi, he sent the prince to receive the commanders and share the hardships of the camp.

sentences.zh: 除秘書郎，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary gentleman but did not accept the office.
translations.idiomatic: He was named secretary gentleman but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 授輔國將軍，遷晉熙王撫軍主簿。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Assists the State and transferred to serve as steward to the General Who Pacifies the Army under Prince Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Assists the State and moved to be chief clerk on Prince Jinxi's pacifying staff.

sentences.zh: 事寧，世祖遣太子還都。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Emperor Wu sent the crown prince back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored, Emperor Wu sent the prince back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖方創霸業，心存嫡嗣，謂太子曰：「汝還，吾事辦矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was then founding his hegemony and kept the legitimate heir in mind. He told the crown prince: 「When you return, my task is done.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng was then laying the foundations of rule and had the succession at heart. He told the prince, 「When you return, my work is finished.

sentences.zh: 」處之府東齋，令通文武賓客。

translations.literal: 」He lodged him in the east study of the princely residence and allowed him access to civil and military guests.
translations.idiomatic: 」He quartered him in the east study of the princely residence and opened the doors to guests civil and martial alike.

sentences.zh: 敕荀伯玉曰：「我出行日，城中軍悉受長懋節度。

translations.literal: He charged Xun Boyu: 「On days when I go out, all troops in the city shall obey Zhangmao's command.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Xun Boyu, 「On days when I leave the city, every soldier in the capital shall answer to Zhangmao.

sentences.zh: 我雖不行，內外直防及諸門甲兵，悉令長懋時時履行。

translations.literal: Even when I do not go out, let Zhangmao from time to time inspect all inner and outer guards and the armored men at every gate.
translations.idiomatic: Even when I stay in, let Zhangmao walk the inner and outer watches and the armored guards at every gate.

sentences.zh: 」轉秘書丞，以與宣帝諱同，不就，改除中書郎，遷黃門侍郎，未拜。

translations.literal: 」He was transferred to secretary director, but since that title matched the taboo name of Emperor Xuan of Jin, he did not take it; he was reassigned as gentleman of the palace secretariat and promoted to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, but had not yet assumed office.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was transferred to secretary director, but the title matched the taboo of Emperor Xuan of Jin, so he declined; he was reassigned gentleman of the palace secretariat and promoted gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, without yet taking office.

sentences.zh: 升明三年，太祖將受禪，世祖已還京師，以襄陽兵馬重鎮，不欲處他族，出太子爲持節、都督雍梁二州、郢州之竟陵、司州之隨郡軍事、左中郎將、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming, as the Grand Ancestor was about to receive the abdication, Emperor Wu had already returned to the capital. Because Xiangyang was a key stronghold for troops and horses and he did not wish to place another clan in charge, he sent out the crown prince as bearer of the staff, superintendent of military affairs in the two provinces of Yong and Liang, Jingling in Ying province, and Sui commandery in Si province, left central commander, colonel pacifying the barbarians, and inspector of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming year 3, as Xiao Daocheng prepared to accept the throne, Emperor Wu was already in the capital. Xiangyang held the empire's horses and arms, and he would not trust another house with it—so he sent the prince out as bearer of the staff, superintendent of Yong and Liang, of Jingling in Ying and Sui in Si, left central commander, colonel pacifying the barbarians, and inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，封南郡王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In Jianyuan year 1 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 he was enfeoffed Prince of Nan commandery, fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 江左未有嫡皇孫封王，始自此也。

translations.literal: Never before in the lands south of the Yangtze had a legitimate imperial grandson been enfeoffed as prince; it began with this.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze no legitimate imperial grandson had ever been made a prince before; the precedent began here.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced in title to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His title was raised to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁州刺史范柏年誘降晉壽亡命李烏奴，討平氐賊楊城、蘇道熾等，頗著威名。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fan Bonian, inspector of Liang province, had induced the fugitive Li Wunu of Jinshou to surrender and had crushed the Di bandits Yang Cheng, Su Daoshi, and others, winning considerable renown.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fan Bonian, inspector of Liang, had won over Li Wunu, a Jinshou outlaw, and put down the Di chiefs Yang Cheng and Su Daoshi, until his name carried weight.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，柏年遣將陰廣宗領軍出魏興聲援京師，而候望形勢。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's rebellion arose, Bonian sent his general Yin Guangzong to lead troops out from Weixing to signal support for the capital while watching how events unfolded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, Bonian sent Yin Guangzong out of Weixing with an army, ostensibly to aid the capital while he read the wind.

sentences.zh: 事平，朝廷遣王玄邈代之。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the revolt was crushed, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 烏奴勸柏年據漢中不受命，柏年計未決，玄邈已至，柏年遲回魏興不肯下。

translations.literal: Li Wunu urged Bonian to hold Hanzhong and refuse the order; Bonian had not yet decided when Xuanmiao arrived. Bonian lingered at Weixing and would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wunu urged Bonian to seize Hanzhong and defy the summons. Bonian wavered; Xuanmiao was already on the road, yet Bonian hung back at Weixing and would not descend.

sentences.zh: 太子慮其爲變，乃遣說柏年，許啓爲府長史，柏年乃進襄陽，因執誅之。

translations.literal: The crown prince, fearing he might rebel, sent someone to persuade Bonian, promising to recommend him as chief steward of the princely establishment. Bonian then advanced to Xiangyang, where he was seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, fearing a mutiny, sent envoys promising to name Bonian chief steward of his staff if he came in. Bonian marched to Xiangyang—and was seized and put to death.

sentences.zh: 柏年，梓潼人，徙居華陽，世爲土豪，知名州里。

translations.literal: Bonian was a native of Zitong who had moved to live at Huayang; for generations his family had been local magnates, known throughout the province.
translations.idiomatic: Bonian came from Zitong and had settled in Huayang; for generations his clan had been great landlords, famed in the province.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始中，氐寇斷晉壽道，柏年以倉部郎假節領數百人慰勞通路，自益州道報命。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Song, Di raiders cut the road to Jinshou. Bonian, as gentleman of the bureaus of grain, took the staff of authority and led several hundred men to comfort troops and reopen the route, returning by way of Yizhou to report.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Taishi era Di raiders severed the Jinshou road. Bonian, then gentleman of the grain bureaus, took the staff and led several hundred men to reopen the route and hearten the garrisons, then returned by the Yizhou road to report.

sentences.zh: 除晉壽太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed administrator of Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 討平氐賊，遂爲梁州。

translations.literal: After he had put down the Di bandits, he became inspector of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di were pacified he became inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 柏年強立，善言事，以應對爲宋明帝所知。

translations.literal: Bonian was forceful in bearing and skilled in speech; his ready replies won him notice from Emperor Ming of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Bonian was imposing in person and quick in counsel; Emperor Ming of Song prized his repartee.

sentences.zh: 旣被誅，巴西太守柳弘稱啓太祖，敕答曰：「柏年幸可不爾，爲之恨恨！」

translations.literal: After he was executed, Liu Hong, administrator of Baxi, submitted a memorial to the Grand Ancestor. The edict in reply read: 「It would have been fortunate if Bonian had not come to this; I deeply regret it!」
translations.idiomatic: After the execution Liu Hong of Baxi memorialized Xiao Daocheng. The reply read, 「Bonian might have been spared this—I grieve for it!」

sentences.zh: 時襄陽有盜發古塚者，相傳云是楚王塚，大獲寶物玉屐、玉屏風、竹簡書、青絲編。

translations.literal: About that time grave robbers opened an ancient tomb at Xiangyang; tradition held it was the tomb of a King of Chu. They took a great haul of treasures: jade sandals, a jade screen, bamboo slips bound with green silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: About then robbers broke into an old tomb at Xiangyang said to be a King of Chu's. They carried off jade sandals, a jade screen, bamboo slips, and green-silk bindings in great quantity.

sentences.zh: 簡廣數分，長二尺，皮節如新。

translations.literal: The slips were several inches wide and two feet long; the outer bark joints seemed fresh.
translations.idiomatic: The slips were several inches across and two feet long; the bamboo skin looked newly cut.

sentences.zh: 盜以把火自照，後人有得十餘簡，以示撫軍王僧虔，僧虔云是科斗書《考工記》，《周官》所闕文也。

translations.literal: The robbers held torches to see by. Later someone obtained more than ten slips and showed them to the General Who Pacifies the Army Wang Sengqian; Sengqian said they were tadpole-script "Artificers' Record," text missing from the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The thieves lit torches to read by. Later a man came by a dozen-odd slips and showed them to Wang Sengqian, general who pacifies the army. Sengqian said they were tadpole script, the Artificers' Record—the portion the Offices of Zhou lacks.

sentences.zh: 是時州遣按驗，頗得遺物，故有同異之論。

translations.literal: At that time the province sent men to investigate and recovered many of the relics, hence conflicting accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The province sent investigators and recovered part of the hoard, which is why accounts differ.

sentences.zh: 會北虜南侵，上慮當出樊、沔。

translations.literal: When the northern barbarians invaded south, the emperor feared the court might have to move out toward Fan and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern enemy pushed south, the throne feared it might have to withdraw toward Fan and Mian.

sentences.zh: 二年，征爲侍中、中軍將軍，置府，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: In year 2 he was summoned as palace attendant and general of the central army, with a staff established, and garrisoned at Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was recalled as palace attendant and general of the central army, given a staff, and posted to Stone City.

sentences.zh: 穆妃薨，成服日，車駕出臨喪，朝議疑太子應出門迎。

translations.literal: When Consort Mu died, on the day of completing mourning dress the imperial carriage went out to condole. Court discussion was divided on whether the crown prince should go out to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Mu died, on the day he finished putting on mourning the emperor rode out in person. The court debated whether the prince should go out to meet the carriage.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王儉曰：「尋《禮記‧服問》『君所主夫人妻、太子、嫡婦』，言國君爲此三人爲主喪也。

translations.literal: Left vice minister Wang Jian said: 「If we look to "Dress Questions" in the Book of Rites—"for the lord's wife, the heir apparent's wife, and the chief daughter-in-law, the lord himself presides over mourning"—that means the sovereign presides over mourning for these three.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, left vice minister, said, 「The Book of Rites, "Dress Questions," says the lord himself presides for his wife, the heir apparent's wife, and the chief daughter-in-law—that is, the sovereign leads mourning for these three.

sentences.zh: 今鸞輿臨降，自以主喪而至，雖因事撫慰，義不在吊，南郡以下不應出門奉迎。

translations.literal: Now the imperial phoenix carriage descends; it comes in its capacity as chief mourner. Though there is incidental consolation, the rite is not one of condolence; the Prince of Nan commandery and those below him should not go out to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: Today the imperial carriage comes down as chief mourner. Comfort may be offered on the way, but the visit is not a condolence call; the Prince of Nan and his household should not go out to welcome it.

sentences.zh: 但尊極所臨，禮有變革，權去杖絰，移立戶外，足表情敬，無煩止哭。

translations.literal: Yet where the supreme honor arrives, ritual may bend: for the moment put aside staff and hemp, and stand outside the door—enough to show reverence without requiring one to cease weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the supreme presence arrives, ritual bends: lay aside staff and sackcloth for the moment and stand outside the door—reverence enough without forcing an end to weeping.

sentences.zh: 皇太子旣一宮之主，自應以車駕幸宮，依常奉候。

translations.literal: The heir apparent, as master of his palace, should in any case receive the imperial carriage when it visits his quarters in the usual form of attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent is master of his own palace; when the carriage honors his quarters he should receive it in the usual way.

sentences.zh: 旣當成服之日，吉凶不容相干，宜以衰幘行事。

translations.literal: On a day when mourning dress is completed, auspicious and inauspicious rites must not clash; he should act wearing hemp cap and headband.
translations.idiomatic: On the day mourning dress is completed, joy and grief must not mingle—he should go in hemp cap and headband.

sentences.zh: 望拜止哭，率由舊章。

translations.literal: Stopping tears to perform the bow toward the carriage—all according to established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Cease weeping to bow toward the carriage—that follows old precedent.

sentences.zh: 尊駕不以臨吊，奉迎則惟常體，求之情禮，如爲可安。

translations.literal: Since the supreme carriage does not come for condolence, welcoming it is only the ordinary courtesy. Weighing feeling and rite, that seems acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme carriage does not come to mourn; to meet it is only ordinary courtesy. Judged by feeling and rite, that should suffice.

sentences.zh: 」解侍中。

translations.literal: 」He was relieved of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was relieved of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 上以太子哀疾，不宜居石頭山障，移鎮西州。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the crown prince was in mourning and ill, thought Stone City's mountain defenses unsuitable and moved him to garrison West Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding the prince in grief and poor health, thought Stone City's mountain redoubts unsuitable and shifted him to West Province.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷使持節、都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、征北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was transferred as bearer of the staff of authority, superintendent of military affairs in the two provinces of southern Xu and Yan, general who campaigns north, and inspector of southern Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was transferred bearer of the staff, superintendent of southern Xu and Yan, general who campaigns north, and inspector of southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，爲皇太子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was made crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu acceded, Xiao Zhangmao was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖好《左氏春秋》，太子承旨諷誦，以爲口實。

translations.literal: At first the Grand Ancestor loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; the crown prince carried out his intent by reciting it until it became a favorite topic.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Xiao Daocheng loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; the prince recited it at his bidding until the text lived on his tongue.

sentences.zh: 旣正位東儲，善立名尚，禮接文士，畜養武人，皆親近左右，布在省闥。

translations.literal: Once installed as heir apparent, he cultivated reputation and esteem, received scholars with courtesy, and kept martial men about him—all close at hand, placed throughout the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the eastern palace he courted a fine name, welcomed men of letters, and kept fighting men near—all of them in his inner circle, stationed through the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，於崇正殿講《孝經》，少傅王儉以擿句令太子僕周顒撰爲義疏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming, he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Correct Reverence; Junior Tutor Wang Jian, by selecting passages, had Palace Adjutant Zhou Yong compile a commentary.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 3 he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Correct Reverence; Junior Tutor Wang Jian picked out passages and had Palace Adjutant Zhou Yong draft a commentary.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，太子臨國學，親臨策試諸生，於坐問少傅王儉曰：「《曲禮》云『無不敬』。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year the crown prince attended the National Academy, personally presided over the written examination of the students, and from his seat asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian: "The Qu Li chapter of the Record of Rites says, 'There is nothing to which one is not reverent.'
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the fifth year the crown prince went to the National Academy, sat in person to examine the students, and asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian from his seat: "The Qu Li says, 'There is nothing to which one is not reverent.'

sentences.zh: 尋下之奉上，可以盡禮，上之接下，慈而非敬。

translations.literal: Serving from below upward can exhaust ritual; receiving those below from above is kindness, not reverence.
translations.idiomatic: From below to above one may exhaust every rite; from above to those below there is kindness, not reverence.

sentences.zh: 今總同敬名，將不爲昧？

translations.literal: To use the same name "reverence" for both—will that not obscure the distinction?
translations.idiomatic: To call both by the single name "reverence"—will that not blur what is distinct?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「鄭玄云『禮主於敬』，便當是尊卑所同。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Zheng Xuan says 'Ritual takes reverence as its foundation'—that should hold for superior and inferior alike.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian replied: "Zheng Xuan says 'Ritual takes reverence as its foundation'—then high and low should share it alike.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「若如來通，則忠惠可以一名，孝慈不須另稱。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "If one follows that through, loyalty and generosity could share one name, and filial piety and compassion would need no separate terms.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "If that holds all the way through, loyalty and kindness could be one name, and filial piety and compassion would need no second term.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「尊卑號稱，不可悉同，愛敬之名，有時相次。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Titles for superior and inferior cannot all be identical; the names love and reverence sometimes follow in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "Titles for high and low cannot all match; the names love and reverence sometimes come one after the other.

sentences.zh: 忠惠之異，誠以聖旨，孝慈互舉，竊有徵據。

translations.literal: The difference between loyalty and generosity truly rests on the sage's intent; filial piety and compassion are raised in turn—I have private evidence for this.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and kindness differ by the sage's meaning; filial piety and compassion are set side by side—I have warrant for that.

sentences.zh: 《禮》云『不勝喪比於不慈不孝』，此則其義。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says 'One who cannot bear mourning is like one who is unkind and unfilial'—that is the point.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, 'One who cannot bear mourning is like one unkind and unfilial'—that is the proof.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「資敬奉君，資愛事親，兼此二塗，唯在一極。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Drawing on reverence to serve the ruler and on love to serve one's parents—both paths share a single pole.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "Reverence feeds service to the ruler, love feeds service to parents—both roads meet at one pole.

sentences.zh: 今乃移敬接下。

translations.literal: Yet now reverence is shifted to receiving those below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now reverence is moved down to those below.

sentences.zh: 豈復在三之義？

translations.literal: How can that still accord with the sense of "three"?
translations.idiomatic: How does that still fit the meaning of "three"?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「資敬奉君，必同至極，移敬逮下，不慢而已。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Drawing on reverence to serve the ruler must reach the same pole; extending reverence to those below means only not to be disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "Reverence in serving the ruler must reach the same pole; carrying reverence down to those below means only not to slight them.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「敬名雖同，深淺旣異，而文無差別，彌復增疑。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Though the name is the same, the depth and shallowness clearly differ—yet the text makes no distinction, which only deepens the doubt.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "The name is one, but depth and shallowness differ—and the wording shows no gap, which only adds doubt.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「繁文不可備設，略言深淺已見。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Elaborate wording cannot all be set forth; stated briefly, the depth and shallowness are already plain.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "Full phrasing cannot all be laid out; in brief, depth and shallowness are already clear.

sentences.zh: 《傳》云『不忘恭敬，民之主也」。

translations.literal: The Commentary says 'Never forget reverence and respect—such a one is lord of the people.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, 'Never forget reverence and respect—such a one is lord of the people.'

sentences.zh: 《書》云『奉先思孝，接下思恭』。

translations.literal: The Documents say 'In serving the ancestors, think of filial piety; in receiving those below, think of respect.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, 'In serving the ancestors, think of filial piety; in receiving those below, think of respect.'

sentences.zh: 此又經典明文，互相起發。

translations.literal: Here again is explicit scripture, each passage calling forth the other.
translations.idiomatic: Here again the classics speak plainly, each line drawing the other out.

sentences.zh: 」太子問金紫光祿大夫張緒，緒曰：「愚謂恭敬是立身之本，尊卑所以竝同。

translations.literal: " The crown prince asked Zhang Xu, Minister of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord. Zhang said: "I hold that reverence and respect are the root of taking one's stand in the world—hence superior and inferior share them alike.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince asked Zhang Xu, minister of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord. Zhang said: "I take reverence and respect as the root of standing in the world—that is why high and low share them.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「敬雖立身之本，要非接下之稱。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Though reverence is the root of self-cultivation, it is hardly the term for receiving those below.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "Reverence may be the root of the person, but it is not the name for receiving those below.

sentences.zh: 《尚書》云『惠鮮鰥寡』，何不言恭敬鰥寡邪？

translations.literal: The Documents say 'Be kind to widowers and widows'—why not say 'be reverent and respectful to widowers and widows'?"
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, 'Be kind to widowers and widows'—why not say, 'be reverent and respectful to widowers and widows'?"

sentences.zh: 」緒曰：「今別言之，居然有恭惠之殊，總開記首，所以共同斯稱。

translations.literal: " Zhang said: "When spoken of separately, the difference between respect and kindness is plain; at the opening of a record they are taken together, and therefore share one designation.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang said: "Spoken apart, respect and kindness plainly differ; at the head of a record they are opened together, and so share one name.

sentences.zh: 」竟陵王子良曰：「禮者敬而已矣。

translations.literal: " The prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, said: "Ritual is reverence and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, said: "Ritual is reverence, nothing beyond it.

sentences.zh: 自上及下，愚謂非嫌。

translations.literal: From highest to lowest—I see no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: From top to bottom—I see no problem in that.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「本不謂有嫌，正欲使言與事符，輕重有別耳。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "I never said there was difficulty—I only want words to match affairs, with lighter and heavier clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "I never called it a problem—I only want speech to fit the deed, with light and heavy kept apart.

sentences.zh: 」臨川王映曰：「先舉必敬，以明大體，尊卑事數，備列後章，亦當不以總略而礙。

translations.literal: " The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, said: "To lead with reverence is to clarify the larger frame; the details of rank and ritual are fully set out in later chapters—one should not let a general summary block that.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, said: "To open with reverence is to show the great pattern; the counts of rank and rite are spelled out in later chapters—a summary should not stand in the way.

sentences.zh: 」太子又以此義問諸學生，謝幾卿等十一人，竝以筆對。

translations.literal: " The crown prince again put this question to the students; Xie Jiqing and eleven others all answered in writing.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince put the same question to the students; Xie Jiqing and eleven others all answered in writing.

sentences.zh: 太子問王儉曰：「《周易乾卦》本施天位，而《說卦》云『帝出乎《震》』。

translations.literal: The crown prince asked Wang Jian: "The Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes originally applies to Heaven's position, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says 'The Lord emerges from Zhen.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince asked Wang Jian: "The Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes is set for Heaven's place, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says, 'The Lord emerges from Zhen.'

sentences.zh: 《震》本非天，義豈相主？

translations.literal: Zhen is not Heaven by nature—how can the meanings preside over each other?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen is not Heaven by nature—how can one meaning rule the other?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「《乾》健《震》動，天以運動爲德，故言『帝出《震》』。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Qian is strength, Zhen is motion; Heaven takes motion as its virtue, hence 'the Lord emerges from Zhen.'
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "Qian is firm, Zhen is movement; Heaven's virtue is movement, hence 'the Lord emerges from Zhen.'

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「天以運動爲德，君自體天居位，《震》雷爲象，豈體天所出？

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "If Heaven takes motion as its virtue, the ruler himself embodies Heaven in his station—yet Zhen, Thunder, is the image. How can that be what embodies Heaven's emergence?
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "If Heaven's virtue is movement, the ruler bodies forth Heaven in his seat—yet Zhen, Thunder, is the image. How is that the bodying-forth of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「主器者莫若長子，故受之以《震》。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "He who holds the vessel is none so fit as the eldest son—hence he receives Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "He who holds the vessel—none like the eldest son—so he receives Zhen.

sentences.zh: 萬物出乎《震》，故亦帝所與焉。

translations.literal: All things emerge from Zhen—thus the Lord's portion lies there as well.
translations.idiomatic: The ten thousand things come from Zhen—so the Lord's share is there too.

sentences.zh: 」儉又諮太子曰：「《孝經》『仲尼居，曾子侍』。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian further addressed the crown prince: "In the Classic of Filial Piety, 'Confucius was at rest and Zengzi attended him.'
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian went on to ask the crown prince: "In the Classic of Filial Piety, 'Confucius was at rest and Zengzi attended.'

sentences.zh: 夫孝理弘深，大賢方盡其致，何故不授顏子，而寄曾生？

translations.literal: The principle of filial piety is vast and deep; only a great sage can exhaust its reach. Why was it not given to Yan Hui but entrusted to Master Zeng?
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety runs wide and deep; only a great sage can reach its limit. Why not give it to Yan Hui, but lodge it with Master Zeng?

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「曾生雖德慚體二，而色養盡禮，去物尚近，接引非隔，弘宣規教，義在於此。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Though Master Zeng's virtue fell short of matching the Sage in stature, his nourishing his parents' countenance fulfilled the rites in full; he was still near to things, without a gap in transmission—to spread and proclaim the regulations of the teaching, the point lies here.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "Master Zeng's virtue did not match the Sage in body, yet he nourished his parents' looks to the full of ritual; he was still close to things, with no break in the line—to spread the teaching's rule, the reason is here.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「接引非隔，弘宣雖易，去聖轉遠，其事彌輕。

translations.literal: " Wang Jian said: "Without a gap in transmission, spreading the teaching is easy—but the farther one stands from the Sage, the lighter the matter becomes.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian said: "No break in the line, and spreading the teaching is easy—but the farther from the Sage, the lighter the thing grows.

sentences.zh: 旣云『人能弘道』，將恐人輕道廢。

translations.literal: Since it is said 'it is man who enlarges the Way,' I fear men will slight the Way and let it fall into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: It is said, 'Man can enlarge the Way'—I fear men will slight the Way and let it die.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「理旣有在，不容以人廢言，而況中賢之才，弘上聖之教，寧有壅塞之嫌？

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Since the principle exists, one cannot discard the words because of the man—and when a man of middling talent spreads the teaching of the highest Sage, could there be any suspicion of obstruction?
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "The principle stands—you cannot throw away the words because of the man; and when a middling talent spreads the highest Sage's teaching, is there any fear of blockage?

sentences.zh: 」臨川王映諮曰：「孝爲德本，常是所疑。

translations.literal: " The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, addressed him: "Filial piety as the root of virtue is often in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, asked: "Filial piety as the root of virtue is often doubted.

sentences.zh: 德施萬善，孝由天性，自然之理，豈因積習？

translations.literal: Virtue extends to ten thousand goods; filial piety springs from inborn nature—it is the law of what is natural. How could it depend on accumulated habit?
translations.idiomatic: Virtue pours into ten thousand goods; filial piety comes from inborn nature—the way of what is so. How could it rest on long practice?

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「不因積習而至，所以可爲德本。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Precisely because it is not reached through accumulated habit that it can serve as the root of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "Because it is not reached by practice that it can be the root of virtue.

sentences.zh: 」映曰：「率由斯至，不俟明德，大孝榮親，衆德光備，以此而言，豈得爲本？

translations.literal: " Ying said: "Following this one arrives without awaiting bright virtue; great filial piety brings glory to one's parents and all virtues shine complete—for that reason, how can it be called the root?
translations.idiomatic: " Ying said: "Follow this and you arrive without waiting for bright virtue; great filial piety honors kin and every virtue gleams—on that reading, how is it the root?

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「孝有深淺，德有小大，因其分而爲本，何所稍疑？

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Filial piety has depth and shallowness, virtue has small and great—taking one's portion as root, what room for doubt remains?
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "Filial piety has depth and shallowness, virtue has large and small—each takes its measure as root; what is left to doubt?

sentences.zh: 」太子以長年臨學，亦前代未有也。

translations.literal: " That the crown prince in mature years should preside over the academy was likewise without precedent in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: " A crown prince of mature years presiding over the academy was likewise unheard of in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 明年，上將訊丹陽所領囚，及南北二百里內獄，詔曰：「獄訟之重，政化所先。

translations.literal: The following year the emperor was to review prisoners under Danyang's jurisdiction and jails within two hundred li north and south, and issued an edict: "The weight of imprisonment and litigation comes first in government and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor was to hear cases for prisoners under Danyang and jails within two hundred li north and south, and decreed: "The weight of prison and suit comes first in rule and reform.

sentences.zh: 太子立年作貳，宜時詳覽，此訊事委以親決。

translations.literal: The crown prince has reached the years to serve as second to the throne; he should review these matters in timely detail—this review is entrusted to him for personal decision.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has come to years as second heir; he should look through these in good time—this hearing is entrusted to his own judgment.

sentences.zh: 」太子乃於玄圃園宣猷堂錄三署囚，原宥各有差。

translations.literal: " The crown prince then, in the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings in the Mystic Enclosure Garden, recorded prisoners from the three offices and granted pardons each according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince then, in the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings in the Mystic Enclosure Garden, entered the prisoners of the three offices and granted pardon each in measure.

sentences.zh: 上晚年好游宴，尚書曹事亦分送太子省視。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor favored feasts and outings; business from the Secretariat offices was also divided and sent to the crown prince for review.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor loved feasts and tours; Secretariat business was also split off and sent to the crown prince to review.

sentences.zh: 太子與竟陵王子良俱好釋氏，立六疾館以養窮民。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, both favored Buddhism and established the Six Diseases Hospices to care for the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, both favored the Buddhist teaching and founded the Six Diseases Hospices to nourish the poor.

sentences.zh: 風韻甚和而性頗奢麗，宮內殿堂，皆雕飾精綺，過於上宮。

translations.literal: His bearing was very harmonious, yet his nature was rather luxurious; within the palace, every hall and chamber was carved and adorned with fine brocade, surpassing the upper palace.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was gracious and easy, yet he was extravagant by nature; halls and chambers throughout his palace were carved and hung with fine brocade, outdoing even the emperor's own quarters.

sentences.zh: 開拓玄圃園，與臺城北塹等，其中樓觀塔宇，多聚奇石，妙極山水。

translations.literal: He opened and extended the Mystic Enclosure Garden, equal to the north moat of Jiankang; within it, towers, belvederes, and pagodas gathered many strange stones, achieving landscape to the utmost of wonder.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the Mystic Enclosure Garden to rival the capital's north moat; pavilions, belvederes, and pagodas rose among heaps of curious stone, the landscape wrought to a pitch of artifice.

sentences.zh: 慮上宮望見，乃傍門列脩竹，內施高鄣，造游牆數百間，施諸機巧：宜須鄣蔽，須臾成立；

translations.literal: Fearing the upper palace might see it, he planted tall bamboo beside the gates, set high screens within, and built hundreds of movable wall-sections fitted with every sort of mechanism: when screening was needed, they stood up in a moment;
translations.idiomatic: Lest the imperial palace look down upon it, he lined the gates with tall bamboo, raised high screens within, and built hundreds of touring wall-panels fitted with clever devices—when a screen was wanted, it rose in an instant;

sentences.zh: 若應毀撤，應手遷徙。

translations.literal: if they were to be taken down, they shifted away at a touch.
translations.idiomatic: when they were to come down, they moved aside at a touch.

sentences.zh: 善制珍玩之物，織孔雀毛爲裘，光彩金翠，過於雉頭矣。

translations.literal: He was skilled at making rare curios; he wove peacock feathers into robes whose gold-green brilliance surpassed even zhichidou fur.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at precious novelties and wove peacock down into robes whose gold-green sheen outshone even zhichidou fur.

sentences.zh: 以晉明帝爲太子時立西池，乃啓世祖引前例，求東田起小苑，上許之。

translations.literal: Because when Emperor Ming of Jin was crown prince he had built the Western Pool, he memorialized Shizu citing that precedent and asked to raise a small park on the Eastern Fields; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the precedent of Jin Emperor Ming's Western Pool when he was heir, he petitioned Shizu to build a small park on the Eastern Fields; the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 永明中，二宮兵力全實，太子使宮中將吏更番役築，宮城苑巷，制度之盛，觀者傾京師。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, both palaces' military strength stood at full muster; the crown prince had palace officers and clerks take turns on corvée to build—within the palace city, parks and lanes—the splendor of the layout made all Jiankang stare.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, both palaces kept their forces at full strength; the crown prince rotated palace officers through corvée labor on his works—palace wards, parks, and lanes—until the scale of the layout made the whole capital gape.

sentences.zh: 上性雖嚴，多布耳目，太子所爲，無敢啓者。

translations.literal: Though the emperor's nature was severe and he posted many eyes and ears, none dared report what the crown prince did.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stern by nature and kept many informants, yet no one dared speak of what the crown prince was doing.

sentences.zh: 後上幸豫章王宅，還過太子東田，見其彌亘華遠，莊麗極目，於是大怒，收監作主帥；

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor visited the Prince of Yuzhang's residence and on his return passed the crown prince's Eastern Fields, he saw them sprawling in splendor, magnificent to the horizon, and in great wrath arrested and imprisoned the overseers in charge;
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor called on the prince of Yuzhang; returning by way of the crown prince's Eastern Fields, he saw splendor stretching without end, gorgeous to the horizon, and in a rage had the project overseers seized and jailed;

sentences.zh: 太子懼，皆藏匿之，由是見責。

translations.literal: the crown prince, in fear, hid them all away and was rebuked for it.
translations.idiomatic: the crown prince, afraid, hid them all away—and was rebuked for it.

sentences.zh: 太子素多疾，體又過壯，常在宮內，簡於遨遊。

translations.literal: The crown prince had long been prone to illness, yet his frame was overly stout; he often stayed within the palace and was sparing in outings.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had long been sickly, yet his body was overfull; he kept to the inner palace and went little abroad.

sentences.zh: 玩弄羽儀，多所僭儗，雖咫尺宮禁，而上終不知。

translations.literal: He played with insignia of rank and usurped many prerogatives; though the forbidden precinct lay only a few paces away, the emperor never knew.
translations.idiomatic: He toyed with regalia and overstepped rank in many ways; the palace forbidden zone was only steps away, yet the emperor never learned of it.

sentences.zh: 十年，豫章王嶷薨，太子見上友于旣至，造碑文奏之，未及鐫勒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Ni, died; the crown prince, seeing the emperor's brotherly affection had reached its height, composed an epitaph and presented it, but it was not yet carved.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Ni, died; seeing the emperor's brotherly love at its fullest, the crown prince drafted an epitaph and submitted it, but it had not yet been cut in stone.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月，太子有疾，上自臨視，有憂色。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the eleventh year, the crown prince fell ill; the emperor came in person to visit him, his face troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the eleventh year the crown prince fell ill; the emperor visited him in person, worry plain on his face.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，上表曰：「臣地屬元良，業微三善，光道樹風，於焉蓋闕，晨宵忷懼，有若臨淵。

translations.literal: When the illness turned grave, he submitted a memorial saying: 「Your servant stands in the place of the heir, yet my achievement in the three duties is slight; to illumine the Way and plant custom—there I am wanting; morning and night I am anxious, as one standing over an abyss.
translations.idiomatic: As the sickness deepened he memorialized: 「I hold the heir's station, yet my fulfillment of the three duties is slight; to brighten the Way and set the tone for the realm—there I have failed; dawn to dusk I tremble as at a cliff's edge.

sentences.zh: 攝生舛和，構離痾疾，大漸惟幾，顧陰待謝。

translations.literal: In tending my life I lost harmony and drew on myself this wasting illness; the great transition is near, only a little remains; I turn toward shadow and await departure.
translations.idiomatic: In keeping my health I fell out of balance and brought on this lingering malady; the great change draws near, only a breath remains; I face the shade and wait to go.

sentences.zh: 守器難永，視膳長違，仰戀慈顏，內懷感哽。

translations.literal: To guard the vessel long is hard; to attend your meals will be forever denied; looking up I yearn for your kindly face, and within I choke with grief.
translations.idiomatic: To keep the vessel is not for long; to watch over your meals I must forever forgo; I lift my eyes to your gracious countenance and my throat closes with grief.

sentences.zh: 竊惟死生定分，理不足悲，伏願割無已之悼，損旣往之傷，寶衛聖躬，同休七百，臣雖沒九泉，無所遺恨。

translations.literal: I reflect that life and death are fixed allotments and reason gives no cause for grief; I humbly pray you cut off unending mourning and lessen grief for what is past, treasure and guard your sacred person, share blessing for seven hundred years—even if your servant sinks to the nine springs, no regret will remain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I know life and death are allotted and need not be mourned; I beg you end grief without measure and ease sorrow for what has passed, guard your sacred person, and share fortune for seven hundred years—though I go down to the nine springs, I shall have no regret.

sentences.zh: 」時年三十六。

translations.literal: 」He was thirty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 太子年始過立，久在儲宮，得參政事；

translations.literal: The crown prince had only just passed the age of investiture; long in the Eastern Palace, he had taken part in government affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had only just come of age for investiture; long resident in the Eastern Palace, he had already shared in affairs of state;

sentences.zh: 內外百司，咸謂旦暮繼體。

translations.literal: within and without, every office held that he would succeed before long.
translations.idiomatic: inside and outside the court, every office assumed he would succeed any day.

sentences.zh: 及薨，朝野驚惋焉。

translations.literal: When he died, court and country were struck with shock and regret.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, court and country were shaken with grief.

sentences.zh: 上幸東宮，臨哭盡哀，詔斂以袞冕之服，諡曰文惠，葬崇安陵。

translations.literal: The emperor came to the Eastern Palace and wept there with full grief; he ordered him enshrouded in full ceremonial robes, gave the posthumous title Wenhui, and buried him at Chong'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to the Eastern Palace and mourned with full grief; he ordered the heir enshrouded in full regalia, posthumously titled him Wenhui, and buried him at Chong'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 世祖履行東宮，見太子服翫過制，大怒，勑有司隨事毀除，以東田殿堂爲崇虛館。

translations.literal: Shizu inspected the Eastern Palace, saw the crown prince's garments and curios beyond regulation, and in great anger ordered the offices to destroy them as found and made the Eastern Fields halls into the Chongxu Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu walked through the Eastern Palace, saw the crown prince's dress and playthings far past statute, and in a rage ordered the offices to demolish them on the spot; the Eastern Fields halls became the Chongxu Lodge.

sentences.zh: 鬱林立，追尊爲文帝，廟稱世宗。

translations.literal: When Yulin was established, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen; his temple title was Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin took the throne, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, with the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 初，太子內懷惡明帝，密謂竟陵王子良曰：「我意色中殊不悅此人，當由其福德薄所致。

translations.literal: Earlier, the crown prince inwardly hated Emperor Ming and secretly told the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang: 「In my heart I am wholly displeased with this man—it must be because his fortune is thin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the crown prince had secretly loathed Emperor Ming and told the prince of Jingling, Ziliang: 「Something in my heart utterly rejects this man—surely his merit is thin.

sentences.zh: 」子良便苦救解。

translations.literal: 」Ziliang then pleaded earnestly to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: 」Ziliang then begged hard that he be spared.

sentences.zh: 後明帝立，果大相誅害。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Ming took the throne, he indeed slaughtered many on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Ming acceded, he did indeed kill on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：上古之世，父不哭子。

translations.literal: The historian writes: In high antiquity, a father did not weep for his son.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In high antiquity a father did not mourn his son.

sentences.zh: 壽夭悠悠，尚嗟恆事。

translations.literal: Long or short, life drifts on—yet even that we still lament as the common lot.
translations.idiomatic: Life long or short drifts on—yet even that men still mourn as the common way.

sentences.zh: 況夫正體東儲，方樹年德；

translations.literal: How much more the legitimate heir in the Eastern Palace, just setting out his years and virtue;
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the rightful heir in the Eastern Palace was only beginning to grow in years and virtue;

sentences.zh: 重基累葉，載茂皇家；

translations.literal: a foundation laid through generations, glory heaped on the imperial house;
translations.idiomatic: foundation laid generation on generation, glory heaped on the royal line;

sentences.zh: 守器之君，已知耕稼，雖溫文具美，交弘盛迹，武運將終，先期夙殞，傳之幼少，以速顛危。

translations.literal: a lord who guarded the vessel and already knew the plough—though gentle learning and letters were complete, and he joined in spreading a great record, the martial fortune was near its end, he perished early before his time, and the succession passed to the young, hastening ruin.
translations.idiomatic: an heir who already knew the plough—though his gentle learning was full and he shared in a flourishing age, the martial fortune was ending, he died before his season, and rule passed to a child, hastening collapse.

sentences.zh: 推此而論，亦有冥數矣。

translations.literal: Pushed to this conclusion, there is fate in the dark as well.
translations.idiomatic: Reasoned thus far, there is doom in the unseen too.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：二象垂則，三星麗天。

translations.literal: In praise: The two images hang as law; the three stars adorn heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: The two emblems hang as law; three stars crown the sky.

sentences.zh: 樹嫡惟長，義匪求賢。

translations.literal: The heir is planted by seniority alone; the principle is not to seek worth.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is set by birth order alone; right does not mean choosing the worthy.

sentences.zh: 方爲守器，植命不延。

translations.literal: He had just become keeper of the vessel; the life planted would not extend.
translations.idiomatic: He had only just become keeper of the vessel; the life planted would not run its course.

translations.literal: [1] Endnote marker.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has used as the base for collation the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi (January 1972).
